messages:
maya: FYI I rolled kernel-selector v2 to canary last night. Perf tests show a regression in comm/compute overlap on 8xA100 multi-GPU runs — allreduce tail up ~35% for TP=4, PP=2. attaching quick profile dump

kevin: Can you paste the short nvprof / nsight timeline? curious if streams are serialized or if there's host-sync spikes

maya: pasted timeline below (trimmed):
```
GPU0: stream0 compute kernelA  12.1ms
GPU0: stream1 allreduce    48.3ms
GPU0: stream2 hostSync     3.9ms  <-- suspicious
GPU1: stream0 compute kernelA  12.0ms
GPU1: stream1 allreduce    50.2ms
...
Total per-token latency increased where allreduce no longer overlaps with compute on stream0 in many slices.
```

rachel: this smells like stream affinity/handshake ordering during cudaGraph replay. I hit a similar thing when capture used the compute stream for capture but replay used a different ordering; capture->replay introduced a host-side synchronization at the boundary.

jess: re: kernel-selector v2 — it changed kernel tiling and also switched some kernels to run on 'priority' streams to avoid stalls. Could be a capture vs non-capture stream mismatch. Did the rollout change the stream IDs we pick?

maya: yep selector now prefers "priority" stream for matmul kernels. graph capture code assumes compute kernels stay on default streams. If capture sees priority stream it falls back to host sync during replay.

kevin: can you repro with a minimal runner? try: `./scripts/perf/run_tp.sh --model=llama-7b --tp=4 --pp=2 --batch=2 --stress --trace`

maya: repro command ran, attaching condensed trace (snip):
```
[ 0.012s ] cudaStreamBeginCapture(stream_priority)
[ 0.012s ] launch kernelA on stream_priority
[ 0.024s ] cudaStreamEndCapture(stream_priority)
[ 0.024s ] cudaGraphInstantiate(g)
[ 0.050s ] cudaGraphLaunch(g)  // internally rebinds streams -> causes implicit sync
[ 0.053s ] host thread blocked for 2.7ms
[ 0.055s ] ncclAllReduceAsync(...) on stream_default (now serialized)
```

ops-bot: deploy "kernel-selector v2" rolled to canary at 2361200000 by jess (sha: ab12cde) :rocket:

kevin: OK that trace is useful. Two things to try: 1) force kernel-selector to use default stream (quick test: `REDWOOD_FORCE_DEFAULT_STREAM=1`) 2) change capture logic to always capture on a dedicated capture stream and remap launches into that capture context (so replay doesn't see differing stream attributes).

jess: i can hotfix the selector to prefer default stream for now. if that reduces tail we'll follow up with capture-path change. I pushed a quick toggle: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR_LEGACY_STREAMS=1` to canary.

maya: flip applied. reran repro: tail now down to +5% (from +35%). overlap restored in most slices.

rachel: we should add an explicit test in the graph-replay test harness for mixed-priority-stream captures + nccl async groups. Throw in an env matrix test for `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR_LEGACY_STREAMS` toggles.

kevin: agree. long term: make capture use its own stream with `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(cudaStreamNonBlocking)` + ensure we use `cudaStreamBeginCapture(capture_stream, cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal)` then launch all kernels onto that during capture. Also add `ncclGroupStart()`/`ncclGroupEnd()` around async comm to avoid interleaving.

maya: creating ticket in infra: PERF-1428 to track: "graph-capture: enforce dedicated capture stream + update selector stream defaults". I’ll attach repro and traces.

jess: nice triage everyone. :thumbsup: once infra change is in we should run full perf-suite across all TP/PP combos.

kevin: small note — add a microbenchmark that toggles `cudaGraph` replay path vs direct launch with the same stream layout so we can catch regressions in CI.

maya: added to PERF-1428 checklist. marking this thread resolved-ish for canary. will escalate to staging if we still see noise. :eyes:
